clue.text: Capacity of old vessel reduced by one quarter

indicators.note: a thing reduced by something has that part taken away from it

parts.note: a galleon is an old sailing ship
E, east, is one of the four quarters or points of the compass

explanation.surface: A historic ship has lost a quarter of its carrying capacity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced by' removes E (east, a compass quarter) from GALLEON. 'Capacity' is the definition: a gallon is a measure of volume.
explanation.definitionFit: A gallon is a unit of liquid measure, so it names an amount of volume a container can hold.

clue.text: Atmosphere of a native's capital

parts.note: Roma is the Italian name for Rome, the capital as a native Italian says it

explanation.surface: The mood of an indigenous person's main city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'native's' means what an Italian calls their capital: ROMA, not Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: An aroma is a pervading smell, and atmosphere can mean the air or feel surrounding a place.

clue.text: Existing fashion

parts.note: read as the way or style in which one goes about living, not a current trend

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a current trend; read it as the manner of existing.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's way of living, their habits and choices, is their manner of existence.

clue.text: It's barely required in some colonies

definitions.text: It's barely required in some colonies

parts.words: It's barely required in some colonies
parts.note: naturist colonies require people to go about with bare skin

explanation.surface: Something is scarcely necessary in certain overseas settlements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barely' seems to mean scarcely, but it means with no clothes; the colonies are nudist camps, not overseas territories.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unclothed is the rule in naturist camps.

clue.text: Hack writer produces worthless trifle

parts.note: to hack at someone's shins is to kick
George Bernard Shaw, the Irish playwright

explanation.surface: A jobbing journalist turns out something of no value.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hack writer' reads as one phrase, a drudge journalist, but it splits: hack gives KICK and writer gives SHAW.
explanation.definitionFit: A kickshaw is an old word for a trinket or a fancy but insubstantial dish, something of little worth.

clue.text: Rex at home in children's game

parts.note: Rex is Latin for king, as in royal signatures
from the saying an Englishman's home is his castle

explanation.surface: A dog called Rex is at home playing a kids' game.
explanation.walkthrough: The saying 'an Englishman's home is his castle' turns 'at home' into OF THE CASTLE. In the game, one child holds a mound against the others.
explanation.definitionFit: A playground game in which one child stands on a mound and others try to push them off.

clue.text: Puts things in black and white, in PM's place

definitions.text: Puts things in black and white

explanation.surface: Someone writes things down at the Prime Minister's residence.
explanation.walkthrough: Chequers is the British Prime Minister's country house in Buckinghamshire; to chequer is to mark with a pattern of squares, such as black and white.
explanation.definitionFit: Chequering marks something in alternating squares, and the British premier's official country residence bears the same name.

clue.text: Northerner's relations turned up just the same

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means read from bottom to top, and the result is the same word

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A northern relative arrived nonetheless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relations' means narratives, Norse tales, not relatives; 'turned up just the same' says the word reads the same backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Sagas are old Norse and Icelandic prose stories, so they are accounts told by Scandinavians.

clue.text: Scientist such as Democritus, for one

definitions.text: Scientist such as Democritus, for one

parts.words: Scientist such as Democritus, for one
parts.note: Robert Burton wrote The Anatomy of Melancholy under the pen name Democritus Junior, so a Democritus dissects

explanation.walkthrough: Burton's Anatomy of Melancholy was written by 'Democritus Junior', and the ancient Democritus dissected animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who studies bodily structure by dissection is a scientist of that kind.

clue.text: Intimate what might be done, in fact

indicators.note: the letters are shown as raw material that something else could be made from, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone close hints at what could be achieved in reality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intimate' looks like a verb (to hint) but is the noun, a close friend. 'what might be' asks what DONE IN FACT could be rearranged into.
explanation.definitionFit: A confidante is a woman one confides in, a close friend and trusted companion.

clue.text: Object sometimes dropped on pitch

explanation.surface: Something is now and then let fall onto a playing field.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby a drop goal is scored by dropping the ball and kicking it on the half-volley, so a goal is sometimes 'dropped' on the pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: An aim or target is an object one strives for; in rugby a drop goal is kicked from a ball dropped to the turf.

clue.text: Singing style of latest composition

indicators.note: a composition is something put together, so these letters are assembled in a new order

explanation.surface: The newest piece of music is sung in a particular manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composition' looks musical but is the anagram signal on OF LATEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Falsetto is a way of singing in a voice above the natural range, chiefly by men.

clue.text: One slew the albatross, as a result

explanation.surface: A sailor killed a great seabird and suffered the consequences.
explanation.walkthrough: In Coleridge's Rime of the Ancient Mariner the albatross is killed by a crossbow shot fired upward at the flying bird; the upshot of anything is its result.
explanation.definitionFit: An upshot is the outcome or consequence of events, and also literally a shot aimed upward into the sky.

clue.text: Having started with a will, you'll find it

parts.note: from the proverb where there's a will there's a way

explanation.surface: A determined beginner is assured of success.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'where there's a will there's a way' supplies WAY after A. 'Having started' is the definition, as runners are 'away' once the race is under way.
explanation.definitionFit: Runners or a project are said to be away when they have got going or set off.

clue.text: Waves from snow-covered mountains

explanation.surface: Breakers rolling down from snowy peaks.
explanation.walkthrough: Whitecaps are waves with foaming crests; snowy peaks have white caps.
explanation.definitionFit: Foam-crested breakers on the sea, and literally pale tops such as snow on summits.

clue.text: Transform rear of plane to fly

parts.note: to turn is to change one thing into another
the tail is the back end of an aeroplane

explanation.surface: An aircraft's back section is converted to make it airborne.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fly' looks aeronautical but means flee.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn tail is to run away, and to fly here is to flee.

clue.text: Flower girl covered with stripes

parts.note: a tiger is the animal whose coat is striped
Lily is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A bridesmaid wears a striped dress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower girl' reads as a bridesmaid, but splits: Flower is the definition, girl is LILY.
explanation.definitionFit: The tiger lily is an orange lily with dark spots, a garden plant.

clue.text: Judge in court producing outcry, so to speak

definitions.text: Judge in court producing outcry, so to speak

parts.words: Judge in court producing outcry, so to speak
parts.note: an official on a tennis court calls out when the ball lands beyond the boundary, an out cry

explanation.surface: A magistrate in a courtroom provokes public uproar.
explanation.walkthrough: The court is a tennis court, not a law court, and the 'outcry' is a shout of 'Out!'.
explanation.definitionFit: The official who watches a boundary line calls when a ball is out.

clue.text: Party policy not one's main interest

parts.note: a side is a party or faction in a dispute
a line is a policy, as in the party line

explanation.surface: A political party's programme fails to engage its members.
explanation.definitionFit: A sideline is a secondary activity pursued alongside one's main work.

clue.text: Punish schoolboy spectators

explanation.surface: A pupil is disciplined in front of an audience.
explanation.walkthrough: To gate a British schoolboy or student is to confine them to school grounds as a punishment; the gate is also the attendance at a sports match.
explanation.definitionFit: Gating confines a pupil to college as a penalty, and a match's gate is the crowd paying admission.

clue.text: Ringleader caught by an aged headmaster

indicators.note: the letter is held inside the two-letter word

parts.note: the leading letter of ring
aged means old

explanation.surface: A gang leader is arrested by an elderly school head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught by' places R, the first letter of 'Ring', inside AN. Thomas Arnold was the famous headmaster of Rugby School.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Arnold ran Rugby School in the 1830s, the model Victorian school head.

clue.text: Boatman taking over from pilot

explanation.surface: A sailor relieves the man at the helm.
explanation.walkthrough: George is one of the boating friends in Jerome K. Jerome's Three Men in a Boat, and 'George' is pilots' slang for the automatic pilot.
explanation.definitionFit: Aviators nickname the autopilot after a man's name, and one of Jerome's three men rowing up the Thames shares that name.

clue.text: He may be said to have got the message

definitions.text: He may be said to have got the message

parts.words: He may be said to have got the message
parts.note: a man's name that radio operators say to confirm a transmission was received

explanation.surface: A man might be described as having understood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roger' is radio procedure for 'message received', and it is also a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Radio users say this name to confirm they have received a transmission.

clue.text: Display skill in flying machines

parts.note: to air something is to show it off or display it
craft means skill or expertise

explanation.surface: Pilots show off their expertise in aeroplanes.
explanation.definitionFit: Aircraft is the general term for planes, helicopters and other machines that fly.

clue.text: Delicate basket

explanation.surface: A fragile wicker container.
explanation.definitionFit: Frail means weak or fragile, and a frail is also a rush basket for figs or raisins.

clue.text: Called for orange, peeled?

indicators.note: a peeled fruit has lost its skin, so the word orange loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether an orange should be skinned.
explanation.definitionFit: Rang is the past tense of ring, meaning telephoned or called someone.

clue.text: Systematic though brief in examination

indicators.note: the shortened word is placed inside the examination word

parts.note: a medical is a physical examination by a doctor
tho is the shortened informal spelling of though

explanation.surface: An orderly test, even if a short one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts THO inside MEDICAL, between ME and DICAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Methodical means following an orderly, step-by-step procedure.

clue.text: Drive off from various tees round 25

indicators.note: the mixed letters go round the other piece, enclosing it
various suggests different forms, so the letters of tees are mixed up

parts.note: the answer to clue 25, called

explanation.surface: A golfer drives from assorted teeing grounds around the course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'various' rearranges TEES into ESTE, and 'round' puts it around RANG (25 across), splitting EST and E.
explanation.definitionFit: To estrange is to alienate someone, pushing them away emotionally.

clue.text: My rhymes may be catching, on the surface

definitions.text: My rhymes may be catching, on the surface

parts.words: My rhymes may be catching, on the surface
parts.note: both words of the answer rhyme with my, and the thing they name catches fish while floating on the water

explanation.surface: Verses of mine may prove infectious, at least superficially.
explanation.walkthrough: An angler's floating lure fished on top of the water; each of its two words rhymes with 'my'.
explanation.definitionFit: An angler's artificial insect fished floating on the water catches trout on the surface.
